subject.title: fix(doctor): bound AGENTS.md and root-memory file reads

question: Should doctor deliberately stop automatic root-memory migration when either file exceeds 8 MiB, preserve both files, and require manual repair?
rationale: The cap prevents unbounded buffering but changes an existing migration path into a manual-recovery path for large workspaces; code correctness alone cannot establish whether that cutoff and user experience are acceptable.

options.title: Accept the conservative cutoff
options.body: Keep the 8 MiB limit and no-mutation result, with current-head proof and clear skipped-repair messaging before merge.

options.title: Support larger migrations
options.body: Replace the fixed whole-file cutoff with a bounded streaming or explicitly higher-limit migration design and corresponding upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause the hardening
options.body: Do not merge until the root-memory owner chooses a supported maximum size and recovery experience.

recommendation.title: Accept the conservative cutoff
recommendation.body: Keep the 8 MiB limit and no-mutation result, with current-head proof and clear skipped-repair messaging before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the root-memory migration behavior and are best positioned to assess whether the fixed cutoff preserves its intended recovery contract.
